## Statement

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**Draft, and deliberately unresolved.** This page states *two* candidate
formalizations of the same informal question and does not choose between
them. They are not equivalent, they have different conjectured bound shapes,
and Fork B as usually phrased is refuted below. `category` stays `test` until
someone picks a fork; the page is a decision to be made, not a claim.
:::

[View PDF](pdf/main.pdf) · [Download LaTeX source](latex/main.tex) -- mirrors this page's earlier placeholder statement; see [c/0004](/c/0004/) for the $k=1$ base case this generalizes.

### Setting, common to both forks

As in [c/0004](/c/0004/): fix nonempty finite $\mathcal{K}$ (seeds), $\mathcal{D}$ (inputs), $\mathcal{R}$ (outputs), $K = |\mathcal{K}|$, $D = |\mathcal{D}|$, $R = |\mathcal{R}|$, and let $H \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathsf{Fun}(\mathcal{K}\times\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R})$. Fix $k \ge 1$. Draw $k$ independent seeds $\mathit{sd}_1,\dots,\mathit{sd}_k \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{K}$, all published. Every party is computationally unbounded and receives the entire function table of $H$.

::: {.callout-note title="Definition ($k$-instance public-seed extraction)"}
Given samples $x_1,\dots,x_k \in \mathcal{D}$ and side information $z$, draw a single challenge bit $b \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \{0,1\}$, set
$$
y_{i,0} \leftarrow H(\mathit{sd}_i, x_i), \qquad y_{i,1} \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{R} \quad (1 \le i \le k),
$$
and give $\mathsf{D}$ the tuple $\bigl(H,\ (\mathit{sd}_i)_i,\ (y_{i,b})_i,\ z\bigr)$. Write
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub\text{-}}k} := 2\Pr[b'=b] - 1 .
$$
:::

One bit $b$ is shared across all $k$ instances (all-real versus all-random), not one bit per instance. This is what makes the question non-trivial: $k$ instances give a distinguisher $k$ chances at the same question, so the advantage is expected to *grow* with $k$, and the whole issue is how fast.

### The baseline both forks must beat

::: {.callout-note title="Fact (the $k$-fold hybrid, not in question)"}
Swapping one instance at a time from real to random, and answering each step with [c/0004](/c/0004/)'s corollary, gives
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub\text{-}}k} \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{k} \tfrac{8}{5}\Bigl( \sqrt{\epsilon_i R} + \sqrt{\tfrac{\log_2 D}{K}} \Bigr)
\;=\; k \cdot \tfrac{8}{5}\Bigl( \sqrt{\epsilon R} + \sqrt{\tfrac{\log_2 D}{K}} \Bigr) \ \text{ when all } \epsilon_i = \epsilon .
$$
The reduction is unbounded, so it can sample the other $k-1$ sources itself from the table it already holds. At $k=1$ this is exactly c/0004's corollary, which is why c/0004 `specializes` this statement.
:::

Anything worth stating here has to improve on that linear factor $k$.

### Fork A: $k$ independent sources, each unpredictable

$S_1,\dots,S_k$ are separate sources with mutually independent coins, each given the whole table, with $S_i$ producing $(x_i, z_i)$; write $z = (z_1,\dots,z_k)$. Each $S_i$ is $\epsilon_i$-unpredictable in exactly c/0004's sense: no unbounded $P$ has $\Pr[P(H, z_i) = x_i] > \epsilon_i$.

::: {.callout-important title="Fork A conjecture (shape)"}
There is a universal constant $c>0$ with
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub\text{-}}k} \;\le\; c\,\sqrt{k}\;\Bigl( \sqrt{\epsilon R} + \sqrt{\tfrac{\log_2 D}{K}} \Bigr)
\qquad (\epsilon_1 = \dots = \epsilon_k = \epsilon),
$$
that is, the hybrid's factor $k$ improves to $\sqrt{k}$.
:::

**Why $\sqrt{k}$ is a guess and not a corollary.** For product distributions the generic tensorization runs through Hellinger distance: $\mathrm{H}^2(P^{\otimes k}, Q^{\otimes k}) = 1 - (1-\mathrm{H}^2(P,Q))^k \le k\,\mathrm{H}^2(P,Q)$, and $\mathrm{H}^2 \le \mathrm{SD} \le \sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{H}$, so
$$
\mathrm{SD}(P^{\otimes k}, Q^{\otimes k}) \;\le\; \sqrt{2k \cdot \mathrm{SD}(P,Q)} .
$$
That is $\sqrt{k\delta}$, not $\sqrt{k}\,\delta$: it is *worse* than the hybrid's $k\delta$ unless $\delta$ is already small. Getting $\sqrt{k}\,\delta$ needs $\mathrm{H}^2 = O(\delta^2)$ for this particular pair, which is a statement about how c/0004's bound is attained, not a generic inequality. Settling that is most of the work.

### Fork B: one source, a jointly unpredictable tuple

A single source $S$ outputs the whole tuple $\bigl((x_1,\dots,x_k), z\bigr)$, with no independence assumed between coordinates. The natural unpredictability hypothesis is on the tuple: no unbounded $P$ has $\Pr[P(H,z) = (x_1,\dots,x_k)] > \epsilon$.

::: {.callout-important title="Fork B, naive form: FALSE"}
Under tuple-unpredictability alone, no bound of the shape above can hold. Take $k=2$, let $x_1$ be uniform on $\mathcal{D}$, let $x_2 = d_0$ for a fixed $d_0 \in \mathcal{D}$, and let $z = \bot$. The best predictor guesses $(d, d_0)$ and wins exactly when it guesses $x_1$, so the tuple is $\epsilon$-unpredictable with $\epsilon = 1/D$. But $\mathsf{D}$ holds $H$ and $\mathit{sd}_2$, so it computes $H(\mathit{sd}_2, d_0)$ and answers "real" iff $y_{2,b}$ equals it:
$$
\Pr[b'=b] = 1 - \tfrac{1}{2R}, \qquad \mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub\text{-}}2} = 1 - \tfrac1R .
$$
Fixing $R$ and letting $D, K \to \infty$ drives the conjectured right-hand side to $0$ while the advantage stays at $1 - 1/R$, so no universal $c$ survives. A tuple can be hard to guess whole while one coordinate carries no entropy at all, and one dead coordinate is enough.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Fork B, repaired form (shape)"}
Strengthen the hypothesis to **conditional** per-coordinate unpredictability: for every $i$ and every unbounded $P$,
$$
\Pr\bigl[P\bigl(H,\, z,\, (x_j)_{j \ne i}\bigr) = x_i\bigr] \;\le\; \epsilon .
$$
This implies each coordinate individually is $\epsilon$-unpredictable, but unlike Fork A it allows the coordinates to be arbitrarily correlated. Conjectured bound: the same $c\sqrt{k}(\sqrt{\epsilon R} + \sqrt{\log_2 D / K})$ as Fork A, now with correlation permitted.
:::

### How to choose

Fork A is the weaker claim and the safer statement: independence is a real restriction, and the hybrid baseline is honest there. Fork B (repaired) is the one worth wanting, since correlated sources are what an application actually hands you, and it strictly implies Fork A. Fork B is also where the $\sqrt{k}$ shape is least likely to survive, because correlation is exactly what breaks the product structure the Hellinger argument needs.

The two are not a matter of taste: they are different theorems, and the page should carry one of them, with the other either dropped or minted as its own id.
